## Critique
- claim-1: The slot-presence table and symbolic matrix (1) correctly expose the \(p=2,c=2,i=2,j=2\) deletions. However, the certificate is incomplete in two respects. First, exhaustiveness is asserted rather than proved: one must show that the entire degree-\(d+3\) row lattice is generated by \(r_1,\ldots,r_8\), including products by arbitrary elements of \(A_1,A_2,A_3\). Second, for the fifteen small-\((i,j)\) cases in (4), neither the coordinate matrices \(R_{\mathrm{selected}}\) nor the integral coefficient matrices \(\mathcal C\) are displayed. Defining \(\mathcal C=R_{\mathrm{full}}R_{\mathrm{selected}}^{-1}\) makes the resulting equality tautological and does not provide the requested independent entrywise comparison. Thus the bounded certificate is not yet fully established.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] Prove exhaustiveness by stating
  \[
  J_d=\mathbb Zx_0,\quad J_{d+1}=\mathbb Z\{x_1,y_1\},\quad
  J_{d+2}=\mathbb Z\{\gamma,x_2,z,y_2,\theta\},
  \]
  with unavailable slots omitted, and using
  \[
  A_1=\langle h_1\rangle,\quad A_2=\langle h_2,h_1^2\rangle,\quad
  A_3=\langle h_3,h_2h_1,h_1^3\rangle.
  \]
  Explicitly verify
  \[
  h_2h_1x_0=r_2+r_3,\qquad
  h_1^3x_0=r_4+r_5+2r_6+r_7+r_8,
  \]
  \[
  h_1^2x_1=r_4+r_5+r_6,\qquad
  h_1^2y_1=r_6+r_7+r_8.
  \]
  Then, for each of the fifteen cases in (4), display the available-column \(R_{\mathrm{selected}}\), an independently derived integral \(\mathcal C\), and the literal product \(\mathcal C R_{\mathrm{selected}}=R_{\mathrm{full}}\).
- [computation] Supply an exact-integer script for the twenty threshold representatives
  \[
  (i,j)\in\{2,3\}^2,\qquad
  (p,c)\in\{(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,1),(3,1)\},
  \]
  enumerating horizontal strips, printing \(R_{\mathrm{full}},R_{\mathrm{selected}},\det R_{\mathrm{selected}},\mathcal C\), and verifying entrywise that \(\mathcal C R_{\mathrm{selected}}=R_{\mathrm{full}}\).

## Required revisions
- Replace “arise only from” with a proved row-lattice generation statement.
- Expand (4) into explicit coordinate and multiplication data rather than defining \(\mathcal C\) from the desired equality.
- Retain the conditional box/Schur/Pieri hypothesis and make no parent-theorem claim.
